# Dialog

Figma: [05h. Dialog](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-929) · Family: 05 Feedback · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-01-01

### Dialog

Centered modal card that pauses the screen for one considered decision: optional tone icon or hero image, title, description, optional content slot, Cancel and Confirm. Tone=destructive gives a red confirm for irreversible actions.

Level: organism · Contains: Button, IconButton

Use when:
- Confirm withdrawing or cancelling a reservation or investment (Tone=destructive, confirm label Withdraw)
- Acknowledge a regulatory or Sharia disclaimer before continuing (showCancel=false)
- Celebrate a completed investment with a hero image (showImage=true)
- Small picker or form that does not need its own screen (showContent=true)

Don't use when:
- Non-blocking feedback: use Toast or Banner
- Hints or term definitions: use Tooltip, or Popover for interactive ones
- Mobile bottom-anchored choices or long content: use BottomSheet or Action sheet
- Multi-step flows: use a full screen
- Marketing interruptions: never use Dialog

Accessibility: role=dialog aria-modal with focus trapped and returned; Esc and the close X act as Cancel; confirm label is a specific verb.

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

Dialog is a focused modal card that briefly pauses the surrounding interface to demand a single, considered response from the person - typically a confirm or cancel. It is one of the strongest UI interruptions in the system, so use it sparingly and only when the action being confirmed is significant (destructive, irreversible, or carries financial consequence) or when explicit acknowledgment is genuinely required.

### When to use

- Confirming a destructive or irreversible action (withdraw an investment, delete a saved plan, close an account).
- Asking the user to acknowledge a decision that has financial or legal consequence.
- Announcing a successful, completed action that the user must read before proceeding.
- Capturing brief contextual input that does not warrant a full screen (date picker, small form).

### When NOT to use

- For non-blocking feedback or background notifications - use Toast (05b) or Banner (05c) instead.
- For inline help or hints - use Tooltip (04d) instead.
- For multi-step forms or complex workflows that need their own screen - push to a new route instead.
- To advertise features or interrupt the user with marketing content - never use Dialog for unsolicited content.

### Anatomy

Dialog is a vertical stack inside a rounded card with elevation. From top to bottom: a header row with an optional tone icon (left in LTR, right in RTL) and a close button (mirrored), then the title, then an optional description, then the action row with cancel and confirm buttons (right-aligned in LTR, left-aligned in RTL).

### Component properties

- Size (VARIANT) - sm 320px / md 480px / lg 640px. Defaults to sm.
- Tone (VARIANT) - default (info icon, brand-green confirm) or destructive (alert-triangle icon, red confirm). Defaults to default.
- Direction (VARIANT) - LTR or RTL. Mirrors the header row, action row, and text alignment.
- Title (TEXT) - the headline. Default: "Are you sure?"
- Description (TEXT) - body explanation. Default: "This action cannot be undone. Please confirm before continuing."
- showIcon (BOOLEAN) - toggle the tone-icon circle. Default: true.
- showClose (BOOLEAN) - toggle the close X button. Default: true.
- showCancel (BOOLEAN) - toggle the cancel button. Default: true.
- showDescription (BOOLEAN) - toggle the description text. Default: true.

> **Tip:** Cancel and Confirm button labels are NOT exposed as top-level Dialog properties because the Figma Plugin API cannot forward parent properties to nested instance properties. To change a button label, click into the nested cancelButton or confirmButton and override its Button Title property directly. The default labels match the locale (English for LTR, Arabic for RTL).

- showImage (BOOLEAN) - toggle an edge-to-edge image slot at the top of the dialog. Image height scales with Size variant (120px for sm, 160px for md, 200px for lg). The slot is a gray placeholder rectangle that designers replace by dragging an image onto it or setting an image fill via the right panel. Defaults to false.
- showContent (BOOLEAN) - toggle a custom content slot between description and the action row. The slot is an empty placeholder frame that designers detach the instance to fill with custom content (form fields, list rows, picker options, key-value summaries). Defaults to false.

> **Info:** The dialog's outer frame has no padding - the image slot is edge-to-edge. All padded content lives inside a nested bodySection frame. This separation lets the hero image bleed to the rounded corners of the dialog while keeping the rest of the content properly inset. The variant frame has clipsContent=true so images stay within the rounded corners.

### Sizes

Three sizes accommodate the visual weight of the message. Pick by content density, not by importance - a destructive action with a single-sentence explanation belongs in sm, not lg.

sm - 320px wide

Short confirmations with one sentence of context. Compact spacing (20px padding, 12px between rows). Title at 16px, description at 13px. The default Dialog size - start here.

md - 480px wide

Standard confirmations with two to three sentences of context. The most balanced size for most use cases. Title at 18px, description at 14px. 24px padding.

lg - 640px wide

Dense Dialogs with longer explanations, optional inline content (lists, key-value summaries), or important decisions that benefit from a more substantial visual footprint. Title at 20px, description at 14px. 32px padding.

### Tones

Two tones signal the nature of the action being confirmed. The tone affects the icon color, icon backdrop tint, and the confirm button styling. Cancel button styling and overall card chrome stay constant across tones.

### default - info icon, brand-green confirm

Use for non-destructive confirmations: saving a draft, finalizing an investment, acknowledging a completion. The icon is an "i" in a brand-green-subtle circle. The confirm button uses the standard primary brand-green styling.

### destructive - alert icon, red confirm

Use when the action being confirmed cannot be undone or has meaningful negative consequence. The icon is an alert-triangle in a red-subtle circle. The confirm button uses the warning (red) styling. Pair with strong, unambiguous copy on the confirm button ("Delete", "Withdraw", "Close account") - not "OK" or "Yes".

> **Warning:** Do not invent a "success" or "warning" tone for Dialog. For positive completion feedback that does not block the user, use Toast (05b). For non-modal warnings, use Banner (05c).

### Composition - overlay and scrim

The Dialog component itself does NOT include a scrim/backdrop. The scrim is composed separately when the Dialog appears in a screen mockup. This separation lets the same Dialog component work in screen mockups, in modal previews, and as a standalone visual reference.

### How to compose with a scrim

- Place the Dialog instance on top of the screen content it is interrupting.
- Insert a fill rectangle behind the Dialog, sized to match the full screen frame.
- Set the rectangle's fill to bg/overlay or a manual black at 50–60% opacity (industry standard).
- Center the Dialog horizontally and vertically over the scrim - Figma's align tools or use a Center wrapper frame.

> **Info:** A future Composition asset on this page may pre-compose Dialog + scrim into a ready-to-drop modal block. For now, designers manually compose. Track this in the design system roadmap.

### In context - common dialog patterns

Eight common dialog patterns that Safqah designers reach for, each built by combining the Dialog's eight instance properties. Drop a Dialog instance, toggle the booleans, override the texts, and you have the pattern. For form dialogs and picker dialogs the designer detaches the instance to drop their own content (form fields, list rows) into the content slot.

Basic confirmation

Default Dialog state. Icon + title + description + Cancel/Confirm. Use for non-destructive confirmations: saving a draft, completing a form, finalizing a non-critical setting.

Destructive confirmation

Tone=destructive. Alert-triangle icon + red confirm button. Use when the action is irreversible: cancel an investment, delete a saved plan, close an account.

Hero / celebration (with image)

showImage=true, showIcon=false. Replaces the tone icon with a custom hero image. Use for onboarding milestones, achievement confirmations, success celebrations, deal-purchase confirmations. Designers drop their own image into the gray placeholder slot.

Information only (single action)

showCancel=false. Just an OK / Got it button. Use to confirm a one-way notification the user must acknowledge before continuing: a maintenance window notice, a Sharia compliance disclaimer, a regulatory acknowledgment.

Form dialog

showContent=true. Reveals an empty content slot between description and actions. Designers detach the instance and drop their form fields (input rows, dropdowns, file pickers) into the slot. The Cancel/Confirm buttons act as form submit/cancel.

Picker / list dialog

showContent=true, showIcon=false, showDescription=false. Strips down the chrome so the content slot becomes the focal point. Designers fill the slot with selectable rows (a list of accounts, a list of investment goals, a country picker).

Image hero with single action

showImage=true, showIcon=false, showCancel=false. Image-driven onboarding card with one strong call to action. Use for first-time-user moments, post-purchase celebration screens, marketing-aligned confirmations.

Minimal (no chrome)

showIcon=false, showClose=false. Strips both icon and X button. Use when the content itself carries the visual weight (e.g. a printed receipt preview, an OTP entry where the close X would be redundant).

### Notes from the maintainer

> **Info:** Built 2026-06-09 in Syntropy v2.0 build. 12 variants (Size 3 × Tone 2 × Direction 2). 6 instance properties (Title, Description, showIcon, showClose, showCancel, showDescription).

> **Warning:** Cancel and Confirm button labels are overridden at the nested instance level (click into the button to change its Button Title property). This is a Figma Plugin API limitation - parent component properties cannot forward to nested instance properties via setProperties().

> **Warning:** For LTR variants, body text uses IBM Plex Sans. For RTL variants, body text uses Noto Sans Arabic (because IBM Plex Sans Arabic is not installed in the design sandbox). When this design system ships to engineering, ensure IBM Plex Sans Arabic is bundled - it pairs better with the Latin sibling.

> **Tip:** Drop shadow is composed from two layered shadows - a wide soft outer (y=8, radius=32, alpha 0.16) plus a tight inner (y=2, radius=8, alpha 0.08). Together they create the floating-card elevation. Avoid using a single shadow at higher opacity, which reads as a flat drop and not a true elevation.

> **Info:** For destructive Dialogs, the confirm button uses the Button's State=warning variant (the red destructive styling). The Button library does not have a separate Type=destructive - destructive primary is achieved via State=warning on the primary Type.

> **Tip:** When the user dismisses a Dialog via the X close button, treat it semantically the same as Cancel - do NOT proceed with the action. The close button is for closing the modal, not for confirming the action.
